sources.entry: Future AGI - Open-source self-hostable end-to-end LLMOps platform unifying tracing, evals, simulations, datasets, gateway, and guardrails.

summary.one_liner: Future AGI is an open-source, self-hostable LLMOps platform for building, testing, monitoring, guarding, and optimizing AI agents in one feedback loop.
summary.what_it_does: The platform covers simulation of multi-turn and voice conversations against personas and edge cases, and evaluation with 50+ metrics under one evaluate() call (LLM-as-judge, heuristic, and ML). It provides guardrails with 18 built-in scanners plus 15 vendor adapters, usable inline in the gateway or as a standalone SDK. Monitoring is OpenTelemetry-native tracing across 50+ frameworks with span graphs, latency, and token cost. The Agent Command Center is an OpenAI-compatible gateway with 100+ providers, 15 routing strategies, semantic caching, virtual keys, MCP, and A2A. Optimization offers six prompt-optimization algorithms, with production traces fed back as training data. It runs locally via Docker Compose (Standalone or Distributed) or on Kubernetes via Helm, and Cloud is also offered.
use_cases: Evaluate LLM and RAG answers for groundedness and hallucination
Trace and monitor production AI agents with OpenTelemetry
Simulate multi-turn and voice agent conversations before launch
Add PII, jailbreak, and prompt-injection guardrails to LLM apps
Route requests across many LLM providers through one gateway
Optimize prompts using production trace data
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL shown in README> && cd future-agi
Open the local app, copy API and secret keys from the Keys page
pip install fi-instrumentation-otel, then set FI_API_KEY, FI_SECRET_KEY, FI_BASE_URL
Run register() and instrument your framework, e.g. pip install traceai-openai and OpenAIInstrumentor().instrument()
notable: Single platform spanning simulate, evaluate, protect, monitor, and optimize, with data flowing back into the loop
Apache 2.0 core with inspectable evaluators and prompts rather than black-box scoring
Gateway with published benchmark claims (~29k req/s on t3.xlarge, P99 ≤ 21 ms with guardrails on) and a committed benchmark harness
Standalone and Distributed install modes, plus production Compose overlay and Helm chart
Voice agent simulation and evaluation with LiveKit, VAPI, Retell, and Pipecat
caveats: Standalone install data cannot be migrated to Distributed or Helm later, per the README
Distributed mode needs 4+ vCPUs and 12–16 GB; Standalone needs 2 vCPUs and 4 GB for Docker
Self-hosted installs send deployment telemetry by default (email addresses and domains of admin accounts) unless opted out
AWS Marketplace listing is marked coming soon; air-gapped support requires contacting sales
